clue.text: Birds on course, maybe from Selkirk

parts.note: robins are common garden birds
taken as written

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of course could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Birds flying on their usual course, possibly having come from a place called Selkirk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges COURSE into the second word. Alexander Selkirk, a Scottish sailor marooned on a Pacific island, was the model for Defoe's castaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's shipwrecked hero was drawn from the real experiences of the marooned sailor Alexander Selkirk.

clue.text: Possible clue to premier advertisement is a problem, of course

parts.note: read as wordplay, D, A, M, P set upwards gives PM (prime minister, premier) and AD (advertisement)

explanation.surface: A suggestion for a prime ministerial poster turns into a household problem.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'rising' reverses DAMP to PM AD, so the answer is itself a clue to 'premier advertisement'. Rising damp is moisture creeping up house walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Moisture seeping upwards through walls is a common and costly defect in older houses.

clue.text: Humber is no longer where pressure's high — express good wishes about it

indicators.note: about means the word for good wishes goes around the other piece

parts.note: to bless is to wish someone well
in weather maps a ridge is an elongated area of high pressure

explanation.surface: A remark on the River Humber now crossed, with good wishes around high pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: The Humber estuary in northern England got its suspension bridge in 1981, so it is no longer without one.
explanation.definitionFit: An estuary once lacking any crossing span has had that status ended by a new suspension structure.

clue.text: Tune named after northern Scottish town

indicators.note: after puts the tune and named pieces behind the northern piece

parts.note: an air is a tune
N is an abbreviation for named or name

explanation.surface: A melody called after a town in the north of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Nairn is a coastal town near Inverness.
explanation.definitionFit: A small royal burgh on the Moray Firth in the Highlands of Scotland.

clue.text: See 13
See 1
Inducing tranquillity about directions to having chip on shoulder?

indicators.note: about means the calm word goes around the directions

parts.note: something restful brings calm
E and N are the compass directions east and north

explanation.surface: Calming words given about directions to someone who bears a grudge.
explanation.walkthrough: To have a chip on one's shoulder is an idiom for nursing a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a chip on their shoulder harbours bitterness and a sense of grievance.

clue.text: Rock and rule

definitions.meaning: to move gently back and forth

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both swinging to and fro and power over others.

clue.text: Boy in a whirl

definitions.meaning: a boy's name, a form of Edward
a swirl of water or air turning in a circle

explanation.definitionFit: Both a familiar male name and a small whirlpool or circular current.

clue.text: Top 19 in trauma caused by sword

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the word for a wound

parts.note: a scar is the mark left by a trauma or wound

indicators.note: Top here is a verb, to cut off the head, so the first letter of the word goes

parts.note: the answer to 19 across is a word for a bound or maximum

explanation.surface: Injuries reaching the highest level, caused by a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' is a verb here, meaning behead, not a noun for the highest level; 19 refers to the answer at 19 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved oriental blade, the classic sabre of Persian and Turkish horsemen.

clue.text: See 24
Too much for May term I dole out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Excessive for the summer term, as I hand things out.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something excessively or beyond reasonable bounds.

clue.text: Cad all but stops between Chartres and Angers

parts.note: Nogent-le-Rotrou is a station on the railway from Chartres to Angers

indicators.note: all but means every letter except the last one is used

parts.note: Le Mans is a station on the same line from Chartres to Angers

explanation.surface: A scoundrel nearly halts the journey between two French cities.
explanation.walkthrough: The two stops are Nogent (-le-Rotrou) and Le Mans; 'all but' drops the final S of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A cad is a man who behaves dishonourably, the opposite of a gentleman, in the old idiom.

clue.text: Ammonia used on Catholic house collapse is refined and very affected, supposedly by Selkirk

indicators.note: used in the sense of worn or knocked about, so the letters of ammonia are rearranged

parts.note: RC is the abbreviation for Roman Catholic
a fall is a collapse
taken as written
U means upper-class or refined, from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters of very are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chemical spilled on a collapsed church house is sophisticated and very pretentious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' turns AMMONIA into IAMMONA and 'affected' turns VERY into RVEY. The line opens Cowper's 'Verses Supposed to be Written by Alexander Selkirk'.
explanation.definitionFit: William Cowper put these opening words into the mouth of the marooned sailor Selkirk in his poem.

clue.text: I promote growth, when "I err" is left out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of encouraging growth, provided their mistake is overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges I ERR and IS LEFT together.
explanation.definitionFit: Manure or chemical plant food speaks in the first person, since it promotes the growth of crops.

clue.text: Letter at the end of Nile

definitions.meaning: the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet
the fan of land where the river Nile meets the Mediterranean

explanation.definitionFit: Both a Greek character and the triangular river-mouth landform named after its shape.

clue.text: Order to behave when drunk: take container for tea to point in Derbyshire

indicators.note: a drunk slurs an S into SH, so the order is said that way

parts.note: an ASBO was a British Anti-Social Behaviour Order
an urn holds tea for many cups
E is the compass point east

explanation.surface: A slurred demand to behave, a tea vessel, and a spot in Derbyshire.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO was a British court order against antisocial conduct. Ashbourne is a market town in Derbyshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: A market town at the southern edge of the Peak District, in that Midlands county.

clue.text: Reptile eating cooked fowl with possible cold drink

indicators.note: eating means the reptile word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a snake is a legless reptile

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of fowl are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A serpent swallowing a roasted bird along with something chilly to sip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges FOWL and 'eating' places the result in the reptile; 'cooked' and 'eating' make the surface a kitchen scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A flake of falling snow is frozen water, so in a sense a possible cold drink once melted; it is also a cocktail name.

clue.text: Error in bill spread about one's church

indicators.note: about means the spread word goes around the others

parts.note: marge, short for margarine, is a spread for bread
one is I, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A mistake on an invoice spreads around a person's church.
explanation.walkthrough: MARGE is British slang for margarine; 'spread' looks like a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge wrongly is to make a mistake when billing someone.

clue.text: It follows report of member, as far as it goes

indicators.note: follows puts the word it after the sounded piece
report of signals a word as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a limb, such as an arm or leg, is a member of the body
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark about a member of a club, followed through to its end.
explanation.walkthrough: The B of LIMB is silent, so its spoken form gives LIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A boundary or maximum marks the point beyond which something cannot go.

clue.text: Begin (don't finish) with reason in working order

indicators.note: don't finish means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to open is to begin
rational means having or using reason

explanation.surface: An instruction to start something, but not complete it, sensibly and in good order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don't finish' cuts the N from OPEN, leaving OPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something functioning and ready for use is in working order.

clue.text: Contribution to point-to-point racing is within

indicators.note: Contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something given to an amateur horse race meeting is inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin prefix means inside, as in intravenous.

clue.text: First mother to first father

parts.note: A is the first letter of the alphabet
a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: From the first mother to the first father.
explanation.walkthrough: Eve was the first mother, so the surface invites a biblical pair.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first man was the father of humanity.

clue.text: Deity lives — again

indicators.note: again means the word is given a second time

parts.note: is means lives or exists

explanation.surface: A god lives on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: An Egyptian goddess, wife of Osiris.

clue.text: 1 5's home's worth is a pound plus

parts.note: desert in the sense of what one deserves, as in getting one's just deserts
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra
and means plus

explanation.surface: Someone's house is valued at a pound and a bit more.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 5 is the castaway hero of 1 across, who lived alone for years on an uninhabited isle.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's castaway spent decades marooned on a remote uninhabited isle, which became his dwelling.

clue.text: False set under false set

indicators.note: False suggests the letters of set under are not in their true order

explanation.surface: A fake collection placed beneath another fake collection.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the second 'false set'; the first 'False' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate of artificial teeth is a false set, as opposed to a person's natural teeth.

clue.text: Perfume for alien weapon

parts.note: musk is a strong-smelling scent used in perfumery
ET is the alien of the Spielberg film, and an abbreviation for extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: A scent intended for a visitor from space.
explanation.definitionFit: An old muzzle-loading firearm carried by infantry soldiers.

clue.text: One responsible for setter associated with Lloyd George

definitions.meaning: the parent of the person who set the crossword

explanation.walkthrough: David Lloyd George was a British prime minister; the song 'Lloyd George knew my father' is sung to the tune of 'Onward, Christian Soldiers'.
explanation.definitionFit: A male parent is literally responsible for his child's existence, and the phrase appears in the song title.
